title: Coming soon: my favorite shows of 2025! #theatre #broadway #westend #...
transcript: This is my 2025 theatre wrapped. I saw 173 shows this year, which I believe is a personal record. But hold your applause because actually I've been trying to cut down on theatre, so this is a failure to me. I really hope to never break this record again. I saw 59 shows by myself and the rest with friends, the most being my friend Kat Largent at 16 shows. I saw these shows across 119 different venues, with the most visited being at Luciille Lortel and Classic Stage tied at four. Here you can see several of those venues were not traditional theatres, but rather found spaces like boats, apartments, restaurants, etc. Here we have a breakdown of the types of shows. We have 27 Broadway shows, 11 shows in London, and the rest are various types of shows in New York from off Broadway to festivals found spaces, off off Broadway. About 26% of the shows I saw were musicals or musical adjacent things. 31% were revivals. My most seen playwright was Shakespeare at 8 different productions, and my most seen living playwright was Rajiv Joseph with 3 different productions. My most seen director was David Cromer with a whopping five productions, and that's not even including Dead Outlaw, which I saw in 2024. The longest run time of a show I saw was Initiative at 5h 20m and the shortest was Edelweiss at 45 minutes. Here you can see a list in alphabetical order. Of the 10 different countries of origin that I saw theatre from. Now let's talk about repeats: Just for fun, I included the number of shows where I saw multiple productions of the same material this year, which are Richard II, Tartuffe and Oedipus, but I don't actually count those as repeats. To me, a true repeat is seeing the same production. And I only saw one repeat this year of a show that I had seen already in a past year, which was Aladdin, because I have a friend in the show. As far as seeing the same production twice within the span of 2025, I actually didn't do that at all, which I believe is now the 2nd year in a row. So as I've said many times, I am an outer critics circle voter, which is how I get the majority of my tickets for free. through press agencies. It was at 64.7% of the shows I saw. But here it is removing the press tickets and you can see there's a little bit of rush here and there. I do volunteer ushering, but the two that I wanna draw your attention to most are the “cheap full price” and the “free shows,” because there is a lot more cheap and free theatre in New York than most people realize. But not all of them were cheap, of course. I had 2 tickets that I would label splurges. A $98 ticket to Urinetown at Encore's. don't ask, It was a weird situation. Then a $211 ticket to Masquerade, which is the most expensive ticket I've ever purchased in my life. And these are the price ranges for the rest of the tickets that I paid for. The highest percentage being at $30-$39 And that came to a grand total of $1280.16 for the 32 tickets that I paid for. Here they are broken down by the days of the week. Interestingly, I saw more shows on Mondays than Tuesdays. And the most, of course, being Friday and Saturday. Here they are broken down by month, with April coming in first at 24 shows. And here are the times of day. The earliest was noon, the latest was 9:30. And the most frequent, of course, was 7:00 PM. And here you can see my general reactions in 4 categories. Decisively positive, mixed positive, mixed negative, and decisively negative. Decisively positive doesn't mean it was perfect, and decisively negative, it doesn't mean it was irredeemable. It just refers to my broad overall takeaway. And this is pretty much standard for me. In the past couple years, it's been more like 2/3 vs 1/3 But here it's more like 70% vs 30% So a little bit more positive. Here are some milestones that I hit. A couple of them I already mentioned. But I surpassed 1500 professional productions in my lifetime. 400 Broadway Productions. I Did my 10th annual Weinberg Awards®️, my 1st time voting in the equally prestigious Outer Critic Circle Awards, and I was able to get monetized on TikTok when I passed 10k followers, which I really appreciate that. Plus, of course, I wouldn't be able to be an awards voter and get these press tickets if people weren't following and watching my content, so I really appreciate it. Thanks so much.
classificationReason: Creator presents a '2025 theatre wrapped' covering 173 shows across numerous venues and categories with no single production as the primary focus. Classic roundup.
